scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing the domain controllers, issuing CA, file and database servers, audit repository, the Tier 0 and Tier 1 administration seats, and the offline root CA that this course backs up, rehearses, and records.
scene.completeCaption: Every item in the recovery set has a verified backup, an offline copy under custody, and a rehearsed restore behind it. The recovery record has an owner and a next rehearsal date, and the evidence is ready for course 2.1.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: The directory leads the recovery order. Its scheduled system state and critical-volume backup goes to its own protected volume, and the production Recycle Bin restore in lesson 5 runs against it.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: Keeps its own independent backup, because replication is availability, not recovery. A copy of its virtual machine is the one restored in DSRM on the isolated recovery segment in lesson 5.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · 10.0.30.20
nodes.description: Schedules its own system state and critical-volume backup, and backs up its database, private key, and configuration with certutil and reg export to its protected backup volume. Only the backup’s hashes and custody record go into evidence, and a Tier 0 custodian carries the copy offline.

nodes.name: SBD-AUDIT01
nodes.title: SBD-AUDIT01 · 10.0.50.40
nodes.description: Its hashed log archives are already the protected record. This course adds the archive catalog to the recovery set, and the audit custodian carries a copy to the offline cabinet.

nodes.name: SBD-FS01
nodes.title: SBD-FS01 · 10.0.40.10
nodes.description: Backs up D:\Shares to its protected volume every night, with each file’s NTFS permissions, and keeps an ACL record and share-definition export so access can be checked or reapplied without restoring data.

nodes.name: SBD-SQL01
nodes.title: SBD-SQL01 · 10.0.40.20
nodes.description: A nightly SQL Server Agent job backs up the application databases with master, model and msdb, verified with RESTORE VERIFYONLY. master carries the logins the databases depend on, and the restore note puts it first.

nodes.name: AdminJumpBox01
nodes.title: AdminJumpBox01 · 10.0.60.10
nodes.description: The Tier 0 seat (rule A01). The controllers’ and CA’s backup schedules, the CA backup session, the Group Policy backup task, the Recycle Bin, the Tier 0 closing scans, and the production object restore all run from here.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: The Tier 1 seat. The member-server schedules — SBD-DHCP01, SBD-MGMT01, SBD-REPO01, SBD-SPLUNK01, and the VLAN 40 servers — are set and hashed from here, the audit custodian’s separate sessions reach SBD-AUDIT01, and the member servers’ closing SCAP scans run here.

nodes.name: SBD-ROOTCA01
nodes.title: SBD-ROOTCA01 · Offline, no network address
nodes.description: Stays offline in the vault. Its protected backup from the course 1.6 ceremony is verified and its custody confirmed, never duplicated or copied onto the network.

chapters.network: Everything in the recovery set already runs: both controllers on VLAN 10, the issuing CA on VLAN 30, the audit repository on VLAN 50, the member servers on their own VLANs, the business services on VLAN 40, with SBD-ROOTCA01 offline in the vault. No flows are shown: this lesson writes decisions, and no backup will ever cross the network to reach the offline cabinet.

SBD-DC01, SBD-DC02 and SBD-SUBCA01 now each write a scheduled backup to their own protected volume, and SBD-DC01’s task backs up every GPO, so no backup traffic crosses the network. The flows are the Tier 0 sessions from AdminJumpBox01 on VLAN 60 that set the schedules, take the CA backup, and enable the Recycle Bin.

Each member server writes its scheduled backup to its own protected volume or /srv/backup, set and hashed over Tier 1 sessions from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 — the business services on VLAN 40 among them. SBD-AUDIT01’s archive and catalog join the set through the custodian’s sessions, and no backup crosses the network.

No network flows are shown: the offline backup cabinet has no network path, so copies reach it only by hand. Tier 0 custodians carry the controller, CA, and policy backups, the audit custodian carries SBD-AUDIT01’s archive and catalog, and a Tier 1 custodian carries the member-server sets, the VLAN 40 servers’ included.

The rehearsal runs on the isolated recovery segment, which has no path to the production VLANs and is not drawn here. Back in production, the flow from AdminJumpBox01 to SBD-DC01 shows the Tier 0 session that brings a deleted test object back from the Recycle Bin.

The closing SCAP scans run from each tier’s own seat: AdminJumpBox01 reaches the controllers and the issuing CA, and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 the member servers, SBD-AUDIT01 among them. Every system in the recovery set now has a verified backup, an offline copy, and a place in the recovery record.
